4. //! Bounded LRU cache backed by `BTreeMap`.
5. //!
6. //! Entries are stored in a `BTreeMap` keyed by a caller-chosen type `K` that
7. //! implements `Ord + Clone`. A monotonic counter tracks access order; on
8. //! eviction the entry with the smallest (oldest) counter value is removed.
9. //! Lookups bump the counter to mark the entry as recently used.
10. //!
11. //! # Capacity
12. //!
13. //! The cache is bounded by a capacity given at construction time. When the
14. //! cache is full, the least-recently-used entry is evicted before inserting a
15. //! new one.
16. //!
17. //! # Example
18. //!
19. //! ```
20. //! use cache::Cache;
21. //!
22. //! let mut cache: Cache<&str, i32> = Cache::new(2);
23. //! cache.put("a", 1);
24. //! cache.put("b", 2);
25. //! assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"a").unwrap(), 1);
26. //!
27. //! // Inserting a third entry evicts "b" (least recently used).
28. //! cache.put("c", 3);
29. //! assert!(cache.get(&"b").is_none());
30. //! assert_eq!(*cache.get(&"c").unwrap(), 3);
31. //! ```
32. 
33. #![cfg_attr(not(feature = "std"), no_std)]
34. #![cfg_attr(verus_keep_ghost, feature(proc_macro_hygiene))]
35. #![cfg_attr(verus_keep_ghost, feature(allocator_api))]
36. 
37. //==================================================================================================
38. // Imports
39. //==================================================================================================
40. 
41. extern crate alloc;
42. 
43. use ::alloc::collections::BTreeMap;
44. use ::core::ops::{
45.     Deref,
46.     DerefMut,
47. };
48. 
49. use vstd::prelude::*;
50. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
51. include!("lib.vstd_btree.rs");
52. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
53. include!("lib.spec.rs");
54. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
55. include!("lib.proof.rs");
56. 
57. 
58. //==================================================================================================
59. // Cache Entry
60. //==================================================================================================
61. 
62. /// A single entry in the cache.
63. #[derive(Clone)]
64. struct CacheEntry<V> {
65.     /// Cached value.
66.     value: V,
67.     /// Last-access counter (higher = more recently used).
68.     last_used: u64,
69. }
70. 
71. //==================================================================================================
72. // Cache Guard
73. //==================================================================================================
74. 
75. ///
76. /// # Description
77. ///
78. /// RAII guard providing a reference to a cached entry.
79. ///
80. /// Created by [`Cache::get()`]. Dereferences to `&V` for read access
81. /// and `&mut V` for write access. The LRU counter is bumped when the guard
82. /// is created.
83. ///
84. pub struct CacheGuard<'a, V> {
85.     /// Mutable reference to the cached value.
86.     value: &'a mut V,
87. }
88. 
89. #[verus_verify]
90. impl<V> Deref for CacheGuard<'_, V> {
91.     type Target = V;
92. 
93.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
94.     #[verus_spec(ret =>
95.         ensures *ret == self@,
96.     )]
97.     fn deref(&self) -> &V {
98.         self.value
99.     }
100. }
101. 
102. impl<V> DerefMut for CacheGuard<'_, V> {
103.     fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut V {
104.         self.value
105.     }
106. }
107. 
108. //==================================================================================================
109. // Stdlib Wrappers
110. //==================================================================================================
111. 
112. /// Stdlib wrapper for `BTreeMap::remove`. Needed because `BTreeMap::remove`'s full
113. /// generic signature (`Borrow<Q>`, `Allocator`) is complex. This wrapper fixes Q=K.
114. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
115. #[verus_spec(ret =>
116.     ensures
117.         btreemap_view_spec(*m) == btreemap_view_spec(*old(m)).remove(*k),
118.         ret.is_some() <==> btreemap_view_spec(*old(m)).dom().contains(*k),
119.         ret.is_some() ==> ret == Some(btreemap_view_spec(*old(m))[*k]),
120. )]
121. fn btreemap_remove<K: Ord, V>(m: &mut BTreeMap<K, V>, k: &K) -> Option<V> {
122.     m.remove(k)
123. }
124. 
125. //==================================================================================================
126. // Cache
127. //==================================================================================================
128. 
129. ///
130. /// # Description
131. ///
132. /// A bounded cache using access-counter LRU approximation.
133. ///
134. /// Entries are stored in a `BTreeMap` keyed by `K`. A monotonic counter tracks access order;
135. /// on eviction the entry with the smallest (oldest) counter value is removed. Lookups bump the
136. /// counter to mark the entry as recently used.
137. ///
138. #[verus_verify(reject_recursive_types(K))]
139. #[verus_verify(reject_recursive_types(V))]
140. pub struct Cache<K, V> {
141.     /// Cached entries.
142.     entries: BTreeMap<K, CacheEntry<V>>,
143.     /// Monotonically increasing counter for LRU ordering.
144.     counter: u64,
145.     /// Maximum number of entries.
146.     capacity: usize,
147. }
148. 
149. #[verus_verify]
150. impl<K: Ord + Clone, V> Cache<K, V> {
151.     ///
152.     /// # Description
153.     ///
154.     /// Creates a new empty cache with the given capacity.
155.     ///
156.     /// # Parameters
157.     ///
158.     /// - `capacity`: Maximum number of entries the cache can hold.
159.     ///
160.     #[verus_spec(result =>
161.         ensures
162.             result@ == CacheView::<K, V>::spec_new(capacity as nat),
163.             result@.inv(),
164.     )]
165.     pub const fn new(capacity: usize) -> Self {
166.         let result = Self {
167.             entries: BTreeMap::new(),
168.             counter: 0,
169.             capacity,
170.         };

170.         };
171.         proof! {
172.             Self::lemma_new_view(&result, capacity);
173.         }
174.         result
175.     }
176. 
177.     ///
178.     /// # Description
179.     ///
180.     /// Looks up a cached value and bumps its LRU counter on hit.
181.     ///
182.     /// # Parameters
183.     ///
184.     /// - `key`: The cache key to look up.
185.     ///
186.     /// # Returns
187.     ///
188.     /// An RAII guard providing access to the cached value, or `None` on cache miss.
189.     ///
190.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
191.     #[verus_spec(result =>
192.         requires
193.             old(self)@.inv(),
194.         ensures
195.             // Hit: key is present.
196.             old(self)@.contents.dom().contains(*key) ==> {
197.                 &&& result is Some
198.                 &&& result->Some_0@ == old(self)@.spec_get(*key).1.unwrap()
199.                 &&& self@ == old(self)@.spec_get(*key).0
200.                 &&& self@.inv()
201.             },
202.             // Miss: key is absent.
203.             !old(self)@.contents.dom().contains(*key) ==> {
204.                 &&& result is None
205.                 &&& self@ == old(self)@
206.             },
207.     )]
208.     pub fn get(&mut self, key: &K) -> Option<CacheGuard<'_, V>> {
209.         if let Some(entry) = self.entries.get_mut(key) {
210.             self.counter += 1;
211.             entry.last_used = self.counter;
212.             Some(CacheGuard {
213.                 value: &mut entry.value,
214.             })
215.         } else {
216.             None
217.         }
218.     }
219. 
220.     ///
221.     /// # Description
222.     ///
223.     /// Inserts a value, evicting the least-recently-used entry if at capacity.
224.     ///
225.     /// # Parameters
226.     ///
227.     /// - `key`: The cache key to insert or update.
228.     /// - `value`: The value to store.
229.     ///
230.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
231.     #[verus_spec(
232.         requires
233.             old(self)@.inv(),
234.         ensures
235.             self@ == old(self)@.spec_put(key, value),
236.             self@.inv(),
237.     )]
238.     pub fn put(&mut self, key: K, value: V) {
239.         // A zero-capacity cache cannot store entries.
240.         if self.capacity == 0 {
241.             return;
242.         }
243. 
244.         // If the key is already present, update in place.
245.         if let Some(entry) = self.entries.get_mut(&key) {
246.             self.counter += 1;
247.             entry.value = value;
248.             entry.last_used = self.counter;
249.             return;
250.         }
251. 
252.         // Evict the LRU entry if at capacity.
253.         if self.entries.len() >= self.capacity {
254.             self.evict();
255.         }
256. 
257.         self.counter += 1;
258.         self.entries.insert(
259.             key,
260.             CacheEntry {
261.                 value,
262.                 last_used: self.counter,
263.             },
264.         );
265.     }
266. 
267.     ///
268.     /// # Description
269.     ///
270.     /// Removes a specific key.
271.     ///
272.     /// # Parameters
273.     ///

Now examining the actual issues. The counter field is a u64 that gets incremented in both get and put operations without any overflow protection, which is a real concern since these are external_body functions where Verus can't validate the arithmetic.

The key insight here is that while 2^64 operations is practically unreachable, the spec doesn't account for counter bounds at all. When the counter wraps around, the implementation's behavior would diverge from what the spec claims — the external_body contract says the operation succeeds unconditionally, but overflow could cause the actual behavior to differ. This represents a soundness gap in the verification.

Now I'm moving on to the second issue about whether `get` and `put` could avoid using `get_mut`. The challenge is that `get` needs to update the `last_used` counter while reading the entry, which requires mutable access.

The API design itself is the constraint here — since `get` returns a mutable guard that holds a reference into the BTreeMap, there's no way around needing `get_mut`. You could theoretically redesign the API to return a cloned value instead of a guard, which would sidestep the verification issues, but that would change the public semantics and might not be acceptable depending on the use case.

For `find_lru_victim`, the problem is that Verus has no specifications for BTreeMap iterators, so there's no way to verify a manual loop over one. Even though BTreeMap supports iteration, the verification layer can't reason about it, which is why the external_body is necessary here.

Looking at the axiom for `cache_lru_of_remove`, it describes filtering the LRU ordering when a key is removed, but proving this requires iterating through entries to establish the sorting relationship — something that can't be done without the uninterpreted function.

Now I'm checking whether `contains_key` is actually used in the code. The `get` method uses `get_mut` directly, and I need to verify what `put` does to see if `contains_key` is called anywhere.

Scanning through the implementation, `get` and `put` both use `get_mut`, `evict` calls `find_lru_victim`, `remove` uses the `btreemap_remove` wrapper, and `clear` just clears the entries. So `contains_key` isn't used anywhere in the actual code.

Now I'm examining the specification for `btreemap_remove` to check if it's sound. So `btreemap_remove` returns `Option<V>`, and when called on `self.entries: BTreeMap<K, CacheEntry<V>>`, it instantiates to return `Option<CacheEntry<V>>`. The spec `btreemap_view_spec(*old(m))[*k]` also gives us `CacheEntry<V>`, so that's consistent. Since both `remove` and `evict` ignore the return value anyway, this checks out. It's marked as `external_type_specification` without `external_body` because `CacheEntry` is straightforward enough for Verus to reason about directly—no opaque types hiding inside. That's why it doesn't count toward the 8 external_body declarations.

Your analysis is thorough and substantively correct on the 8 external_body items, 5 assume_specifications, AST mismatches, and the "cannot eliminate" justifications.
